title: Safe use of pesticides
text: Always read the label. Use the exact dose and wait for the safety period before harvest. Wear a mask, gloves and full clothing while spraying. Never spray against the wind, in strong wind, or when rain is expected within a day. Do not eat, drink or smoke while spraying. Wash your hands and clothes afterwards and never reuse empty pesticide containers for food or water. Keep pesticides away from children and animals.

title: Best time to spray
text: Spray in the early morning or evening when it is calm, the temperature is moderate and no rain is expected for at least 24 hours. Avoid spraying in the hot afternoon, in strong wind, or just before rain because the medicine will drift or wash off.

title: Integrated pest management
text: Look at your field every week. Use healthy seed, crop rotation, clean fields, sticky traps, pheromone traps and neem-based sprays first. Use chemicals only when the pest crosses the damage level and as advised by an agriculture officer. This protects friendly insects such as spiders, ladybirds and wasps.

title: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE)
text: To prepare a 5% neem seed kernel extract, crush about 50 grams of neem seed kernels for each litre of water, soak overnight, filter through a cloth, add a little soap to help it stick and spray in the evening. Neem oil at 3 to 5 ml per litre of water with a little soap is another common option. Neem works best on young insects and is safer for the environment.

title: Soil testing and Soil Health Card
text: Test your soil before every season at a government soil testing lab or through your agriculture office. The Soil Health Card tells you which nutrients are low so you can apply the right fertiliser and avoid waste. Add farmyard manure, compost or vermicompost every year to improve soil.

title: Organic manures
text: Farmyard manure, compost, vermicompost and green manure crops such as sunhemp or daincha improve soil structure and water holding. Use only well-decomposed manure. Biofertilisers such as Rhizobium for pulses and Azospirillum or phosphobacteria for cereals can reduce chemical fertiliser use.

title: Saving irrigation water
text: Drip or sprinkler irrigation saves water and fertiliser. Mulching with straw or dry leaves reduces evaporation and weeds. Irrigate in the early morning or evening. Water most carefully at the critical stages of each crop, such as flowering and grain filling. In rice, alternate wetting and drying saves water.

title: Seed treatment and quality
text: Use certified seed of a variety recommended for your area and season. Treat seed before sowing with Trichoderma or Pseudomonas, or as advised by your agriculture officer, to protect young plants from soil-borne diseases. Do a simple germination test before large sowings.

title: Crop rotation and mixed cropping
text: Rotate cereals with pulses or oilseeds to break pest and disease cycles and to improve nitrogen in the soil. Growing border or trap crops such as marigold can reduce some pests.

title: Safe grain storage
text: Dry grain well in the sun before storage, to about 12 to 14 percent moisture for most cereals. Store in clean, dry, rat-proof bins or bags kept off the floor and away from walls. Check regularly for insects and moisture.

title: Heavy rain and waterlogging
text: Open drainage channels before heavy rain. Do not apply fertiliser or spray just before heavy rain because it will wash away. After waterlogging, drain the field quickly, and apply a light dose of nitrogen when the soil is workable if the crop looks yellow. Watch for fungal diseases afterwards.

title: Heat stress
text: In very hot weather irrigate in the early morning or evening, use mulch, avoid applying fertiliser in the hot afternoon, and do not spray during peak heat. Provide shade nets for nurseries and vegetables if possible.

title: Where to get expert help
text: Call the Kisan Call Centre toll-free on 1800-180-1551 to speak to an agriculture expert in your language. You can also visit your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or the block agriculture office for advice, soil testing and approved varieties.

title: Weed management
text: Weeds compete with the crop for water, light and nutrients, especially in the first third of the crop's life. Weed on time by hand, weeder or hoe, mulch, and use clean seed. Use herbicides only as advised for your crop and follow the label.
